title.title: Undistillability of Werner states from three, four and five copies

description_scope.text:
A Werner state is three-copy distillable exactly when it is one-copy distillable. For every local dimension d ≥ 3, the Werner state ρ(d,α) = (I + αF)/(d² + αd) is three-copy distillable if and only if α < −1/2. The same threshold for two-copy distillability was proved in July 2026, and the qutrit case of the three-copy problem had been settled by an archived certificate.
In every dimension we prove four-copy undistillability for α ≥ −79/160 and five-copy undistillability for α ≥ −9/20; for qutrits (d = 3) the bounds improve to −0.4979 and −0.47. Applied to disjoint groups of copies, the results for up to five copies give k-copy undistillability for α ≥ −11/(5k) when k ≥ 6, again in all dimensions. The endpoint α = −1/2 remains open from four copies on, and numerically the four-copy relaxation is not exact there.
By a criterion of P. Costa Rico, each statement is equivalent to an inequality for complex matrices of rank at most two. We prove these inequalities with quartic moment relaxations and exact rational certificates. For three copies there is one certificate for each dimension up to 16, and one certificate whose entries are polynomials in 1/d covers every dimension d ≥ 9. For four and for five copies, one certificate each covers all dimensions from 1.25·10⁹ and from 10¹⁰ on, respectively, and zero padding passes both results to all smaller dimensions. The bound for many copies comes from a linear program over averaged partial-trace norms, with exact rational certificates.
Version 3 adds results on the zeros of the endpoint form. For two copies, the range and co-range of any matrix at which the form vanishes lie in tensor products of two-dimensional subspaces, and each such plane carries a zero; in dimension four this gives all equality cases of a singular-value bound for Kronecker sums. For any number of copies the form is nonnegative near its generic zeros of this kind and, when it is nonnegative for one copy fewer, near product zeros. If k − 1 copies are settled, a failure at k copies would first appear below the endpoint, at a minimiser whose range and co-range have equal local supports of dimension at least three. A quantitative conjecture that would imply undistillability for all numbers of copies is stated and proved for two copies on one class of planes.
The record contains the paper, seven verification packages with the certificates, verifiers and checks, and two Lean 4 formalizations: of the three-copy result for d = 3, …, 8, checked by Lean's kernel alone, and of the four-copy qutrit bound, in which the checks of the certificate identity are evaluated by compiled code.
